children: , the PC and enterprise-infrastructure company, launched its $999 XPS Googlebook with Gemini at the center of the experience. Shares rose about 1.4% to $556.55 Wednesday, based on Tuesday's $548.92 close. Dell is taking its premium laptop brand into Google's push for AI-powered PCs.

The 13-inch machine pairs a Snapdragon X Elite processor with up to 32GB of memory and an on-device AI processor. It also brings Android phone files, messages and apps onto the laptop. Dell says the battery can last up to 16 hours of streaming under its test conditions. According to Reuters' report on the wider Googlebook launch, Dell is one of several PC makers joining Google's premium laptop effort.

The harder question is what buyers will pay for. The picture puts Dell's $556.55 share price 140.89% above its $231.04 GF Value estimatea wide gap that gives investors reason to demand results. Dell has offered no sales or margin target for the new XPS. For now, the laptop is a bid to win premium PC customers; sales will show whether Gemini helps it earn the price.

title: Dell Gains 1.4% as $999 Googlebook Tests Consumer AI Margins
